messages:
sarah-support: FYI customer 'AcmePayments' opened a ticket — their Redwood Private control-plane mTLS to control.acme.internal is failing intermittently since they swapped to a new NAT gateway yesterday.
ivan-netops: can you paste the client-side error and any packet captures? basic checks: DNS, route, and allowlist first.
sarah-support: client log shows repeated: \"TLS handshake failed: no peer certificate\" then timeout. They ran openssl and got:```
$ openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-private:443 -servername control.acme.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
139774...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
---
no peer certificate
---
```
(They redacted IPs.)
lee-se: that alert usually means the server got a ClientHello but didn't accept the client cert/CA chain. But because this is mTLS we also need to check if something is intercepting or re-writing TLS (corporate TLS-inspection). Any chance the new NAT box does TLS interception or changes MSS?
ivan-netops: customer says the NAT is a vendor-managed appliance (WAN edge) with TLS inspection + TCP MSS clamping enabled by default. can you get a packet capture from the client egress? tcpdump from their side attached (trimmed):```
09:12:03.120000 IP client > control: Flags [S], seq 1000, win 29200, options [mss 1400,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
09:12:03.120123 IP control > client: Flags [S.], seq 2000, ack 1001, win 28960, options [mss 1460,...], length 0
09:12:03.120200 IP client > control: Flags [P.], seq 1001:1600, ack 2001, length 599
09:12:03.120210 IP client > control: Flags [P.], seq 1600:2400, ack 2001, length 800
09:12:03.120300 IP control > client: Flags [R.], seq 2001, ack 2400, length 0
```
elaine-engr: interesting — the ClientHello here is split across two segments (599 then 800). Many TLS-inspecting middleboxes drop or fail to reassemble fragmented ClientHellos. If the middlebox tries to interpret/rewrite TLS and only sees the first fragment it might send a RST.
tim-oncall: do we see corresponding logs on the control plane for that customer's source IP? deploy-bot: control-plane log: `bad_client_hello: client_hello_incomplete` from x.x.x.x
lee-se: that matches. Two likely root causes: 1) the new NAT box is doing active TLS inspection and failing to properly proxy fragmented ClientHello, or 2) MSS/TCP segmentation/clamping changed and fragments are being dropped by an upstream firewall.
sarah-support: customer confirms they enabled TCP MSS clamping to 1200 as a default policy on the new appliance. They also enable TLS-intercept for PCI scoping.
ivan-netops: repro steps we asked them to try: 1) temporarily disable TLS inspection for control.redwood-private IPs (or trust our certs), 2) disable MSS clamping / set PMTU discovery, 3) collect a fresh tcpdump while reproducing. Any change after they toggled TLS inspection?
sarah-support: they disabled TLS inspection for the control plane IPs and... handshakes started succeeding immediately. They reported stable connections for 20+ minutes.
elaine-engr: so the middlebox was failing to proxy the fragmented ClientHello. We should recommend either: - whitelisting our control-plane FQDN/IPs to bypass TLS inspection, or - increase PMTU/disable MSS clamping so ClientHello fits in a single segment, or - ensure the appliance properly reassembles TLS records (vendor bug).
lee-se: can we also provide the control-plane IPs and certificate chain they should expect so they can add an allowlist? list: control.redwood-private: 34.198.11.22, 34.198.11.23 (example), cert CN=control.redwood-private, issuer=Redwood Internal CA. (customer confirmed these match.)
tim-oncall: adding a note — if whitelisting isn't allowed for PCI, they must have vendor patch or set the TLS inspection policy to not modify or drop fragmented records. Also ask them to disable any 'early reassembly' feature.
sarah-support: customer will keep TLS inspection off for the control plane. They also opened a ticket with the appliance vendor about MSS clamping + TLS reassembly. Marking support ticket as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
ivan-netops: thanks — can we add a KB entry? short runbook: 1) symptom: intermittent mTLS handshake failures after WAN edge change. 2) likely cause: TLS inspection + TCP MSS clamping causing fragmented ClientHello to be dropped. 3) checks: tcpdump for fragmented ClientHello, openssl s_client shows 'no peer certificate' or 'alert certificate unknown', control-plane logs `client_hello_incomplete`. 4) mitigations: whitelist control-plane, disable TLS inspection for that flow, disable MSS clamping/enable PMTU, vendor firmware patch.
lee-se: agreed. I'll add the KB and link to this thread.
deploy-bot: incident-note: customer AcmePayments - mTLS failures due to TLS-inspection + MSS clamping. Resolved by disabling TLS inspection for control-plane IPs. Ticket closed.
